_authored.by: Claude Fable 5.2, live in a Claude Code session, in Andy Martin's voice

lede: A caps-only display font, drawn from the lettering in the old Bethlehem Steel wordmark. The wordmark only gives you seven letters. I drew the rest from the rules those seven follow.
banner_note: Bethlehem's mill on the Indiana side of Lake Michigan. They never drew a U, N, R, A or O in this style, so most of this line is my guess.
origin: I took this picture at a Bills game on November 22, 2026. The banner hangs in the Blue Moon Bar at Highmark Stadium (Oxford Pennant, out of Buffalo, made it) and I wanted to know what font it was. It isn't one. The letters are hand-cut felt, copied from the mark Bethlehem Steel put on its own catalogs. So I went looking for the catalogs.
origin_caption: Oxford Pennant banner, Blue Moon Bar, Highmark Stadium. Photo: Andy Martin.
charset_intro: 344 glyphs, which covers Google Fonts Latin Core - accented capitals for most of Europe, with the lowercase keys typing the same capitals. The seven red letters are the ones in the catalogs. Everything in black is mine.
rules_intro: Three rules come straight off the seven original letters. I added a fourth for the accents, since Bethlehem never needed one.
rule1: Where a stem ends in open space, it gets cut on a rising diagonal, low on the left. Where it joins another stroke it stays square. You can see it on the T, H and M.
rule2: Where an arm ends in open space, its outside edge runs a little longer than the inside (56 units). Top arms kick up, feet kick down. That's from the E and L.
rule3: Anything that would be round is a rectangle with the corners clipped off. The B and S work that way in the original, so the O, the numbers and even the ring accent do too.
rule4: The accents are cut the same way as the letters: slabs for the acute and grave, two small periods for the dieresis, chevrons for the circumflex and caron, a zigzag for the tilde. I kept them low and wide. I think letters this heavy can carry that, and tall accents would have pushed the lines apart.
languages_intro: A few of the languages it covers.
sources_intro: The catalog covers, all on the Internet Archive. I drew mostly from the 1961 one.
